On an RTX 5070 it decodes at ~59 tok/s fully GPU-resident and validates useful context at 32K, but fails frozen reliability gates under its default xhigh thinking (budget exhaustion, not fabrication) - NOT_READY on this reasoning-on profile. A paired study against a practical Qwen3.8-27B reference finds near-parity on 48 mechanically-scored tasks with a narrow fluent-fabrication tail; the same artifact also runs on an 8 GB RTX 2060 SUPER at 8K context (19.9 tok/s decode). Configuration is part of the result: the separately profiled thinking-off configuration classifies READY_WITH_GUARDRAILS in the follow-up event.

events.profile_name: llama.cpp upstream official Q8_0 (reasoning-on, vendor default)
events.headline: iFlytek's SparkLLM Spark-X2.5-4B is a 4.1B hybrid-attention model (3:1 sliding-window:full attention, 512-token window) advertising a native 1M-token context. On an RTX 5070 with the official Q8_0 GGUF under upstream llama.cpp b10999 it decodes at ~126 tok/s and prefills a 128K window at ~4,300 tok/s; 131,072 tokens is the measured fit ceiling (f16 KV at 36,864 B/token; the advertised 1M maximum needs ~38.7 GB of KV alone - FIT_LIMIT). Useful context validates at 32K/64K/128K in the declared thinking-off lane, but the vendor-default thinking mode consumes the standardized 512-token output reserve at every rung and 0/20 frozen reliability tasks complete on either seed - budget starvation, not fabrication (0 UNSAFE; semantic capability 30/33 clean on the non-starving lane). Campaign execution is COMPLETE_PASS; the model classifies READY_WITH_GUARDRAILS: vendor-default reasoning behavior is budget-sensitive, thinking-off is a materially different practical surface, and the measured useful-context envelope on this hardware is not the model-card native maximum.
